Its not related. The lines being cited are just the place where Godot prints errors that come from shader compiling/linking. So any problem with any shader is going to come from those same lines. 

You don't have the ability to test on the affected device do you? Since it is using SwiftShader, my guess is that the device may not even exist. Swiftshader is a software implementation of Vulkan, so it looks like this is running OpenGL over Vulkan on the CPU using Swiftshader. So its pretty far removed from any real device. 

Also, I think the IllegalStateException is likely a different error altogether and is not related to the fragment shader failing to link. If the Scene shader fails to compile/link, it shouldn't impact your game at all except for printing that error on startup

I did a little more digging. That device has 261 fragment uniform vectors available (https://opengles.gpuinfo.org/displayreport.php?id=6452). By default the fragment shader uses 69 uniform vectors if all features are used (omni lights, spot lights, directional lights, shadowmap etc.). The only way for the shader to use more than that is if the `rendering/limits/opengl/max_lights_per_object` project setting is increased past its default of 8. 

For the renderer to use more than 261 fragment uniform vectors, the setting would have to be set to 105 or higher. 

Accordingly, I think the fragment shader error is most likely an internal bug in SwiftShader.

Since it is using SwiftShader, my guess is that the device may not even exist. Yes, It's not device I own. It's a google's device that does something with the uploaded aab. The only way for the shader to use more than that is if the rendering/limits/opengl/max_lights_per_object project setting is increased past its default of 8. JFYI. I've never touched those settings. I don't use any custom shaders or lights. > If the Scene shader fails to compile/link, it shouldn't impact your game at all except for printing that error on startup > ... > Accordingly, I think the fragment shader error is most likely an internal bug in SwiftShader. It’s not critical for me I think, as I don’t get any errors or warnings in the Play Console after the upload is processed. Most likely, it was already happening before 4.5 — I’ve just started using Sentry to catch it now and got me by surprise. Errors are scary. Warnigs are the stuff to ignore! 😊

I started using Sentry and got these exact same errors for the same device when I made an internal release.

> I started using Sentry and got these exact same errors for the same device when I made an internal release.

I don't think you need to worry about it. I've done a little more searching and confirmed that this device is basically an internal CI check done by Google. Unless they are making a fuss about the error you can basically ignore it since no device out in the wild will be using the SwiftShader OpenGL implementation (it runs on the CPU, so it is super slow). 

SwiftShader doesn't have full OpenGL ES 3.0 compliance. So it's not surprising that there is a bug in the shader compiler.
